lifecycle.creation_reason: Recorded but never given an owner in MT-119.lifecycle.implementation_result.disclosed_gaps: 'AC-119-4 result-row instance left open ... Candidate for a follow-up MT.' Created here so the disclosure is not lost when MT-119 closes.
lifecycle.ready_for_validation_summary: MT-122 implemented. TWO defects, both fixed. (a) STATIC CHROME: three action rows used a plain ui.horizontal with HARDCODED desired_width values (220.0 and 120.0). At a narrow pane those rows overflowed, and egui's Region::expand_to_include_rect widens a Ui's max_rect over the overflow, so the static row handed EVERY later row a layout width larger than the visible pane. Fixed with horizontal_wrapped plus a fit_width(ui, preferred) helper that clamps to ui.available_width(). (b) RESULT ROW: hit.title is unbounded backend content laid out FIRST left-to-right, so a long title consumed the row and pushed the [source_kind] badge past the pane's right edge, where the results ScrollArea clips it - the operator loses the only at-a-glance signal distinguishing a document hit from a file or loom_block hit. Fixed with MT-119's existing idiom rather than a second pattern: reserve the bounded badge first against the row's right edge via Layout::right_to_left, then let the title truncate into what remains, keeping the full title recoverable through egui's show_tooltip_when_elided. PT-122-2 RED (result-row fix reverted, verbatim): 'MT-122: the [source_kind] badge must render FULLY INSIDE the Find-in-Files pane. rect x=[1132.125, 1183.906] y=[198.000, 208.000] vs pane x=[0.000, 420.000] y=[0.000, 800.000]' - the badge rendered 712px outside a 420px pane. PT-122-2 GREEN (fix applied, verbatim): 'test find_in_files::tests::mt122_result_row_badge_stays_inside_the_find_pane ... ok'. PT-122-3 REGRESSION: the full find_in_files suite is 48 passed / 0 failed, and critically mt119_saved_search_controls_stay_inside_the_find_pane is still green, proving the static-chrome change did not regress MT-119's guard. The RED capture reverted ONLY the result-row fix and restored it through a shell trap, so a failed run could not strand a reverted fix on disk. The guard carries five interlocks that refuse to pass vacuously: I0 fails loudly if the STATIC row regresses (so a future reader is not sent to the wrong file), I1 proves the pane is genuinely bounded using clip_rect rather than the Frame response rect which grows to include overflow, I2 proves the fixture title genuinely overflows at 1.5x the pane width, I4 proves truncation is actually in force, and I5 proves the row's content-derived click route is byte-identical so the layout fix did not change the interaction contract. Implementer evidence only, not validation.
ready_for_validation_v4_open_items: PT-122-1 asks for a mounted frame OPENED and described. The guard measures AccessKit bounds from a real two-pass mounted render rather than inspecting pixels, so a validator wanting a visual frame should capture one with HANDSHAKE_GPU_SCREENSHOT=1, which is now proven to work on this host.
MT-113 test_author_id_budget was not executed: it is cfg(feature="integration") and needs a live handshake_core backend, which does not currently compile while the SurrealDB port is in progress.

scope.summary: Bound the Find-in-Files rows that can still overflow a narrow pane: the static action row, which drags later rows off-pane with it, and the result row, where a long hit title pushes the [source_kind] badge out of view.

defect_detail.finding_source: MT-119 AC-119-4 sibling-row survey, which deliberately checked the neighbouring rows rather than declaring them safe by assumption.
defect_detail.verbatim_disclosure: Result rows have NO clippable control - the ENTIRE row is the click target (inner.response.interact(Sense::click())) - so no control can be lost. However a long hit.title CAN push the [source_kind] badge out of view, which is the same defect class at lower severity.
defect_detail.why_it_was_deferred: MT-029 holds mounted visual baselines on this exact pane. Altering the result-row layout mid-WP risked disturbing those baselines for a badge rather than for a control, so it was recorded rather than silently called safe.
defect_detail.severity: Lower than MT-119: no interactive control becomes unreachable. The operator loses a source-kind signal, not an action.
defect_detail.safe_rows_already_cleared: The 'Saved searches' heading is static RichText with no user content. The excerpt line renders in a vertical layout so it wraps rather than pushing sideways. Both were checked and are safe; only the result row is open.

second_defect_found_while_proving_MT119_.status: MEASURED, NOT INFERRED, while implementing the MT-119 PT-119-3 guard on 2026-08-12.
second_defect_found_while_proving_MT119_.finding: At a 420px pane the Find-in-Files STATIC action row overflows on its own, before any user content is involved: find-in-files.save-bookmark (Bookmark Search) renders at x=[388.00, 496.41] and find-in-files.cancel at x=[402.28, 448.59], against a pane right edge of 420.
second_defect_found_while_proving_MT119_.propagation_mechanism: egui Region::expand_to_include_rect widens a Ui max_rect (not only min_rect) to cover that overflow. Every row laid out AFTER the static chrome therefore receives a layout width larger than the visible pane. The saved-search Restore/Remove controls consequently land at x=[380.16,433.28] and x=[441.28,496.41] - outside a 420px pane EVEN WITH THE MT-119 FIX APPLIED.
second_defect_found_while_proving_MT119_.why_it_is_a_distinct_defect: MT-119 fixed user-content-driven overflow in the saved-search row. This is chrome-driven overflow: it needs no user content at all, and it degrades every row below it. Fixing it is a product change and was correctly out of MT-119 scope.
second_defect_found_while_proving_MT119_.guard_already_in_place: The MT-119 guard ships interlock I0 asserting the static-chrome premise, so if this defect worsens the test reports that static chrome outgrew the pane rather than falsely blaming the saved-search layout. That interlock is the tripwire this MT should turn green at a narrow pane.

acceptance_criteria: AC-122-0: at a realistically narrow pane (420px or narrower), the STATIC action row fits inside the pane, and the rows below it are no longer handed a layout width larger than the visible pane. Prove it by setting the MT-119 guard pane width to that narrow value and showing its I0 interlock and the containment assertions pass, where today they cannot.
AC-122-1: with a hit title long enough to overflow the row, the [source_kind] badge remains fully visible inside the Find-in-Files pane at the tested viewport.

AC-122-2: the full title stays RECOVERABLE by the operator (elide with a tooltip, wrap, or equivalent). Truncating so two results become indistinguishable is not an acceptable fix - this mirrors AC-119-2.
AC-122-3: MT-029 mounted visual baselines are re-run and either unchanged, or the change is inspected, described and explicitly re-baselined with the reason recorded. Do not silently re-baseline.
AC-122-4: the whole row remains a single click target - the interaction contract must not change while fixing the layout.
AC-122-5: a non-vacuous containment guard for the badge, in the style established by MT-119 PT-119-3 (bounded viewport, measured pane rect, proven to go RED when the fix is reverted).
proof_targets: PT-122-1: a mounted frame at a realistic long hit title, OPENED and described, showing the badge inside the pane.
PT-122-2: the containment guard shown RED with the fix reverted and GREEN with it applied, both outputs captured verbatim.
PT-122-3: MT-029 visual proofs and MT-113 author-id proofs still green.
scope.risk_if_missed: A search result whose source cannot be identified at a glance degrades the operator's ability to distinguish hits across pillars, and leaves a known, written-down overflow class unowned after MT-119 closes.
